recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS REPORT IS TO EXIMINE THE WORK PERFORMED AT LAS FUENTES RESTRAUNT / BAR / NIGHT CLUB AT 2552-2558 N. HALSTED. SPECIFICALLY, THE FIRST FLOOR(S) OF EACH OF 3 BUILDINGS (2552, 2554 AND 2558) HAVE BEEN COMBINED INTO A SINGLE VENUE. THE1ST FLOOR (NORTH) WALL HAS BEEN COMPLETELY REMOVED FROM 2552. BOTH THE SOUTH AND NORTH (1ST FLOOR) WALLS OF 2554  HAVE BEEN REMOVED. THE SOUTH WALL OF 2558 HAS BEEN BREACHED INTO THE OPEN SPACE OF 2552 / 2554. THERE IS NO VISABLE REPLACEMENT STRUCTURAL MEMBERS TO SUPPORT THESE BUILDING AFTER THE REMOVAL OF THESE VITAL LOAD BEARING WALLS. A CRITICAL EXAMINATION IS REQUIRED THAT MAY WELL REQUIRE THE REMOVAL OF INTERIOR WALL COVERINGS DURING THIS EXAMINATION.SECTION 14X-3-303.1.1.

recent_violations.ordinance: Failed to remove obstruction from exitway that hampers travel and evacuation.  (13-160-070, 13-196-080)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THERE ARE 3 FRONT AND 3 REAR EXIT DOORS AT THIS RESTARAUNT / BAR / NIGHT CLUB. THE VIOLATIONS REGARDING EGRESS OBSTRUCTION FALL INTO 2 CATEGORIES AT THIS VENUE. THE FIRST PROBLEM IS THERE ARE NO CRASH BARS AT ANY OF THESE DOORS AT THIS HIGH OCCUPANT CAPACITY VENUE. EACH DOOR HAS A THUMB LATCH. THE SECOND AND EXTREMELY DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS OBSTRUCTION IS THE POLICY / PROCEDURE AT THIS VENUE. MANAGEMENT, AS A MATTER OF POLICY, INSTRUCTS ALL SECURITY PERSONEL TO KEEP ALL EXIT DOORS LOCKED WHILE THE VENUE IS OPEN FOR BUSINESS. THIS INSANELY DANGEROUS POLICY WAS WITNESSED BY THIS INSPECTOR. UPON ARRIVAL, THIS TASK FORCE ENTERED THE VENUE AFTER THE SECURITY GAURD UNLOCKED 1 OF 3 FRONT DOORS. THE OTHER 5 EXIT DOORS WERE LOCKED AND THE DOOR WE ENTERED WAS RE-LOCKED AFTER WE ENTERED. SECURITY WAS INSTRUCTED BY THIS INSPECTOR TO IMMEDIATELY UNLOCK ALL EXIT DOORS. THEY REFUSED. THIS INSPECTOR THEN PERSONALLY OPENED / UNLATCHED ALL 6 EXIT DOORS. THIS INSPECTOR THEN DID A 10 MINUTE INSPECTION OF THE BASEMENT AND FOUND THE SECURITY STAFF HAD RE-LOCKED ALL 6 EXIT DOORS. AGAIN, THIS INSPECTOR, FOR THE 2CD TIME, UNLOCKED ALL EXIT DOORS. THEN, FOR THE 3RD TIME, MANAGEMENT INSTRUCTED SECURITY TO RE-LOCK ALL EXIT DOORS. AT THIS POINT, THE VENUE WAS CLOSED BY ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER.ALSO, AT THE REAR PATIO AREA, ONE OF THE EXIT GATES WAS PADLOCKED.SECTION 14X-5-505.1.2.

recent_violations.ordinance: Performed or allowed work to be performed without submitting plans prepared, signed and sealed by a licensed architect or registered structural engineer for approval and without obtaining a permit to perform the work.  (13-32-010, 13-32-040, 13-40-020, 13-12-050)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS INSPECTION CONCERNS A RESTAURANT / NIGHT CLUB / BAR KNOWN AS LAS FUENTES. THIS CLUB / BAR / RESTAURANT IS ACTUALLY COMPRISED OF THE 1ST FLOOR AREAS OF 3 SEPARATE, DISTINCT BUILDINGS (WITH 3 SEPARATE ADDRESSES) THAT HAVE BEEN COMBINED, AT THEIR 1ST FLOORS, INTO 1 SINGLE VENUE. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS, THE NORTH EXTERIOR WALL AT THE 1ST FLOOR OF 2552 HAD TO BE REMOVED AS WELL AS THE SOUTH EXTERIOR WALL AT THE 1ST FLOOR OF 2554. IN ADDITION TO THESE TWO COMPLETE (1ST FLOOR) REMOVAL OF EXTERIOR WALLS, THE NORTH EXTERIOR WALL OF 2554 WAS ALSO REMOVED TO JOIN / BREACH INTO THE 2558 FIRST FLOOR SPACE. THE SOUTH EXTERIOR WALL OF 2558 REMAINS, BUT HAS BEEN BREACHED BY A DOUBLE GLASS DOOR WALL OPENING. NONE OF THIS WORK WAS APPROVED BY EITHER THE DEPARTMENT OF ZONING OR THE DEPARTMENT OF BUILDINGS. THERE ARE NO PLANS OR PERMITS ON FILE FOR ANY OF THIS WORK. THERE IS NO APPLICATION TO THE DEPARTMENT OF ZONING TO REQUEST THE JOINING OF 3 BUILDINGS AT THE 1ST FLOOR TO CREATE 1 RESTAURANT / BAR / NIGHT CLUB. ALSO, THERE HAS BEEN EXTENSIVE ELECTRICAL AND PLUMBING WORK DONE WITHOUT PLANS OR PERMITS AT BOTH THIS VENUE AND THE LARGE (REAR) PATIO AREA. THE REAR PATIO AREA HAS A LARGE ARRY OF PERGOLAS CONSTRUCTED (45 LINEAR FEET X 15 FEET IN HEIGHT X 10 FEET IN WIDTH). ALSO, THERE ARE NO PLANS OR PERMITS ON FILE FRO A NEW REAR EXTERIOR PORCH FRON THE REAR ROOF AREA OF 2552 TO THE 3RD FLOOR OF 2552.ALSO. THERE ARE NO PLANS OR PERMITS ON FILE FOR THE REAR ROOF TOP DECK AT 2552.ALSO, THERE HAS BEEN EXTENSIVE INTERIOR WORK PERFORMED TO THE DWELLING UNITS AT 2552 AND 2554.ALSO, THERE ARE NO PLANS / PERMITS OR LICENSES FOR THE REAR PATIO AREA AND THE 2 LARGE REAR PATIO AREA TENTS.ALSO, THE 2CD FLOOR OF 2558 HAS BEEN DUPLEXED INTO THE ATTIC WITHOUT PLANS OR PERMITS.ALSO, THE ATTIC AT 2554 HAS BEEN CONVERTED INTO AN APARTMENT.THIS VENUE HAS BEEN ISSUED A CLOSURE ORDER BY THE DOB.SECTION 14X-4-401.1.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ENLARGE, REHABILITATE, ALTER AND/OR CHANGE THE OCCUPANCY WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING A PERMIT.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE OCCUPANCY WAS AS FOLLOWS.1ST FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.2ND FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.3RD FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.A SUBSEQUENT  PERMIT SEARCH FOUND WATER RECORDS THAT INDICATE A DIFFERENT OCCUPANCY.THE FIRST FLOOR HAD A FRONT COMMERCIAL UNIT AND A REAR RESIDENTIAL UNIT.THE SECOND FLOOR HAD FRONT AND REAR DWELLING UNITS.THE THIRD FLOOR HAD FRONT AND REAR DWELLING UNITS.ALL LEVELS WERE REHABILITATED AND MODERNIZED, NEW FLOOR LAYOUT INTRODUCED BY COMBINING FRONT AND REAR UNITS INTO A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT PER FLOOR. OTHER ALTERATIONS, SUCH AS THE BRICK-IN DOOR OPENING AT THE EAST ELEVATION, AND THE ADDITION OF A DECORATIVE CONCRETE BLOCK GARAGE CONSTRUCTED AT THE REAR OF THE LOT, WERE PERFOMED WITHOUT PLANS AND PERMITS.DUE TO THE EXTENSIVE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS, COUPLED WITH OCCUPANCY CHANGES AFFECTING ALL DISCIPLINES, A DETAILED ARCHITECTURAL PLAN IS NOW REQUIRED TO LEGALIZE ALL ALTERATIONS AND/OR CONSTRUCTION.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Provide
recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ENLARGE, ALTER, REHABILITATE AND/OR CHANGE THE OCCUPANCY WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING A PERMIT.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE FOLLOWING-BUT NOT LIMITED TO, ALTERATIONS WERE OBSERVED.1.-THE FIRST FLOOR BUSINESS UNIT AT GRADE WAS DIVIDED INTO 2 INDEPENDENT APARTMENTS, PARTITIONS WERE ERECTED TO FORM, FULL KITCHENS, FULL BATHROOMS, LIVING/DINING AREAS, LAUNDRY CLOSETS AND BEDROOMS. 2.-THE EAST ELEVATION STORE FRONT WINDOWS WERE REPLACED WITH A BRICK WALL THAT INCLUDES SMALLER RESIDENTIAL WINDOWS.3.-A STEEL STAIR SYSTEM WAS ERECTED AT THE WEST ELEVATION FROM THE ROOF TOP OF THE EXTENDED 1-STORY AREA.4.-THE WEST PORCH SYSTEM WAS ENCLOSED AND THE DECKS WERE ADDED AS ADDITIONAL LIVING SPACE FOR THE 2ND AND 3RD FLOOR APARTMENTS.A SUBSEQUENT PERMIT SEARCH DIDN'T IDENTIFY ANY PERMITS FOR THE MENTIONED ALTERATIONS. ALL DISCIPLINES AFFECTED, ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING, STRUCTURAL/CARPENTRY AND HVAC.SUBMITT A DETAIL ARCHITECTURAL PLAN AND OBTAIN REQUIRED PERMITS TO LEGALIZE OR TO RESTORE BUILDING TO IT'S ORIGINAL USE AND LAYOUT.

In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
